cuadrilla: Finally the bull was too tired from so much bad sticking and folded his knees and lay down and one of the cuadrilla leaned out over his neck and killed him with the puntillo.
Zurito spoke to two of the other lads of the cuadrilla and they ran out to stand back of Manuel with their capes.
Two of the cuadrilla were back of him, with their capes ready to flop over the fence to distract the bull.
“You line up your cuadrilla, so I can see what I’ve got.”

The members of the cuadrilla, who had been watching the burlesque from the runway between the barrera and the seats, came walking back and stood in a group talking, under the electric light in the patio.
The cuadrilla had stepped away from the bull and waited with their capes.
cuadrillas: The youths of the cuadrillas were behind, their heavy capes furled over their arms.

Heads up, swinging with the music, their right arms swinging free, they stepped out, crossing the sanded arena under the arc-lights, the cuadrillas opening out behind, the picadors riding after, behind came the bull-ring servants and the jingling mules.
